evaluation.checkpoint_rule: the candidate is evaluated at the checkpoint of the iteration A017 was evaluated at (900, the iter key inside A017 model_best.pt); finalize reward pick kept as training/model_best_by_reward.pt. G-A032 was evaluated at iter 700 vs 900.

sentinel_tolerance.note: same as G-A030, not calibrated against replay noise; exceeding it means remeasure the baseline, not a verdict on the candidate

target.decides: criterion 1 only; a target-stage failure is final for this arm

reasons.G1:forward_fast:101: flat gait at the fastest command: does the stronger speed push keep a normal gait
reasons.G4:slope_plus_20:101: target: speed and body height on the 20 deg climb (T2)
reasons.G5:stairs_15_up:101: side effect: stairs under a stronger speed push. This case starts on the top platform and walks down first (plan 9); 1.2->1.4 cut 10cm 2-step ascents 10-11 -> 3-5

why: A017 walks well on flat ground (G1/G2 survival 1.0, tracking >= .89). Off flat ground it is slow:
rough_forward and DR at .25-.30 m/s for a .5 m/s command (plan 8-1).
G7 is not lost to the randomisation: DR tracking equals rough_forward tracking on the same terrain,
and heavier robots are not slower (mass-speed r +.05..+.36). It is lost to walking speed on rough ground.
The only lever that raised rough_forward and DR on all three evaluation seeds is track 1.2 -> 1.4
feet_air_time 0.01 (G-A031, same iter 900) moved them both ways; G-A032 (0.1) was evaluated at iter 700.
1.5 is the Isaac Lab v2.3.1 Go2 rough value and the guidebook lecture 14 example.
Risks pre-registered from the same direction: slope crouch-stalls 0 -> 4-8, a lateral push case with
3 terminations, 10cm two-step stair ascents 10-11 -> 3-5. Step +7%, less than half of 1.2 -> 1.4.
